approaches.name: geotagged mobile data and merged databases for health service verification
approaches.description: Uses Kobo Toolbox geotagged data, barcode scans and merged partner datasets linked to DHIS2 to verify health services and drug delivery. Practices: master health service functionality database with verified data; mobile geotagged data via Kobo Toolbox for third-party monitoring; Geotagged images and barcode scans verifying drug delivery; ICRC georeferenced data triangulation for hard-to-reach monitoring; Kobo Toolbox GPS-stamped monitoring of monitors (GEMS); Merged health service functionality database with analytic dashboard.
approaches.why_innovative: New product: cross-donor verified functionality database - cue: 'data quality' | category Technological; adoption apply; judged in 2 round(s); context expanded; final check: digital core, in_use before 2019

evidence.text: Key monitoring elements will include: (a) Development of a master health service functionality database, capturing development and humanitarian health services across donors;

extra_evidence.text: (b) Collection and development of verified data within database to increase confidence in analysis and reported results and provide measures of partner data quality and reporting accuracy;
(c) Generation of monthly health service functionality bulletin and implementing partner data performance reports;

Innovative technologies such as use of mobile and geotagged data through the Kobo Toolbox platform will be applied to strengthen the quality and comprehensiveness of said third-party monitoring and verification mechanisms.

Moving forward, the new operation will ensure that monitoring mechanisms, such as geotagged images and barcode scans, ensure clarity in the delivery and availability of critical inputs to health services, despite the World Bank’s limitations in being able to conduct hands-on monitoring and supervision.

(e) Modernize verification of delivery of pharmaceuticals: Drug procurement and distribution is currently functioning quite well up until “last mile delivery,” the latter constituting an unsolved problem.

In hard to reach areas where the independent monitor may not be able to access, ICRC will apply enhanced monitoring and data collection approaches that triangulate programmatic and georeferenced data on project implementation and results.

To strengthen monitoring activities in the project zones the project will harness disruptive technologies for FCV contexts in collaboration with the Geo-enabling for Monitoring and Supervision (GEMS) initiative (P167344).
The GEMS method is an ideal add-on to project monitoring as it allows for 'monitoring of the monitors' through a very simple approach28.
Moreover, the date, time and global positioning system (GPS) data cannot be manipulated, allowing to always know when and where the monitoring was active.

Once common definitions for variables are defined, analytical software will be used to clean and merge the respective datasets into one, definitive health service functionality database to produce nationwide analysis on health service availability and functionality.
Over time, this database will be linked to DHIS2 and an analytic dashboard will be built to allow for users to view service availability in locations of interest on their own.

category.rationale: Technological: the database and data verification are the mechanism

sector.rationale: Builds a health service database for administrative monitoring and reporting
